paragraphs.title: Love of Instruction and the Stability of the Righteous

easy.explanation: Proverbs 12:1 says, “Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge.”
easy.q: Who loveth knowledge according to verse 1?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the root of the righteous shall not be moved.”
easy.q: What shall not be moved?

easy.explanation: She “is a crown to her husband.”
easy.q: What is a virtuous woman to her husband?

answers: The first loveth knowledge, while the second is brutish
The first is wicked, while the second is wise
The first lacks bread, while the second is rich
medium.explanation: The verse connects instruction with knowledge and hatred of reproof with brutishness.
medium.q: What is the contrast between the lover of instruction and the hater of reproof?

answers: The righteous are condemned, but the wicked stand
The good man obtains favour, while wickedness cannot establish a man
Both are established by their works
medium.explanation: The good man obtains the LORD’s favour, but a man cannot be established by wickedness.
medium.q: How are the righteous contrasted with the wicked in verses 2–3?

medium.explanation: Reproof is correction or rebuke, which the brutish person rejects.
medium.q: What does “reproof” mean in this passage?

answers: They receive what is beneficial and remain stable
They seek outward honor above all
challenge.explanation: The lover of instruction receives knowledge, while the righteous have a root that is not moved.
challenge.q: What quality links the lover of instruction with the righteous?

answers: One brings honor, while the other brings deep harm
challenge.explanation: The virtuous woman is a crown, but the woman who maketh ashamed is as rottenness in her husband’s bones.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between the virtuous woman and the shameful woman?

answers: Character produces either favor and stability or shame and ruin
Wealth is the measure of every person
The wicked are praised for their plans
challenge.explanation: The verses repeatedly contrast instruction, goodness, and righteousness with wickedness, shame, and instability.
challenge.q: What common theme appears in verses 1–4?

paragraphs.title: Thoughts, Speech, and the House of the Righteous

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The thoughts of the righteous are right.”
easy.q: What are the thoughts of the righteous?

easy.explanation: The mouth of the upright “shall deliver them.”
easy.q: What shall the mouth of the upright do?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 12:7 says, “the house of the righteous shall stand.”
easy.q: What shall stand?

answers: The righteous think rightly, while the wicked devise deceit
The righteous seek harm, while the wicked seek peace
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts right thoughts with the deceitful counsels of the wicked.
medium.q: What is the difference between the thoughts of the righteous and the counsels of the wicked?

answers: The mouth of the upright shall deliver them
It lies in wait for blood
It causes the house to fall
medium.explanation: The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the mouth of the upright delivers.
medium.q: How is upright speech connected with deliverance?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “The wicked are overthrown, and are not.”
medium.q: What happens to the wicked when they are overthrown?

answers: Right thinking and upright speech bring protection and deliverance
They have no connection in the passage
challenge.explanation: The righteous think rightly, and the upright mouth delivers those in danger.
challenge.q: What connection appears between righteous thoughts and upright speech?

answers: Righteousness is linked with endurance, while wickedness ends in ruin
The wicked house is more secure
A house is unrelated to conduct
challenge.explanation: The house of the righteous stands, while the wicked are overthrown and disappear.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between the two houses teach?

answers: Speech intended to harm or destroy
challenge.explanation: The image describes wicked words as a hidden trap seeking another person’s harm.
challenge.q: What is meant by words that “lie in wait for blood”?

easy.explanation: A man “shall be commended according to his wisdom.”
easy.q: According to what shall a man be commended?

answers: He that is despised and hath a servant
He that hath a perverse heart
easy.explanation: The passage says the despised man who hath a servant is better than the self-honoring man without bread.
easy.q: Who is better than the man who honoureth himself and lacketh bread?

easy.explanation: A righteous man “regardeth the life of his beast.”
easy.q: What does a righteous man regard?

answers: Useful provision is better than outward honor without bread
Outward honor is always more important
Both men are described as wealthy
medium.explanation: The verse values a humble man with provision above one who honors himself but lacks bread.
medium.q: What is the contrast between the despised man and the self-honoring man?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “he that is of a perverse heart shall be despised.”
medium.q: What brings a person to contempt in verse 8?

medium.explanation: To till land is to work or cultivate it.
medium.q: What does “tilleth his land” mean?

answers: True worth is shown by wisdom and useful provision, not empty status
Outward honor is the highest good
challenge.explanation: Wisdom, humility, and provision are valued above a proud appearance without bread.
challenge.q: What principle is emphasized in verses 8–9?

answers: By caring for animals and working the land
challenge.explanation: The righteous care for their animals, and the person who tills his land is satisfied with bread.
challenge.q: How do verses 10–11 present practical responsibility?

answers: Mercy and cruelty are revealed by how people treat living creatures
The wicked care better for animals
challenge.explanation: The righteous regard an animal’s life, while the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between the righteous man and the wicked suggest?

paragraphs.title: Work, Traps, and the Return of Speech

easy.explanation: The wicked “desireth the net of evil men.”
easy.q: What does the wicked desire?

easy.explanation: The wicked is snared by the transgression of his lips.
easy.q: What snares the wicked?

answers: Good by the fruit of his mouth
easy.explanation: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth.
easy.q: With what shall a man be satisfied?

answers: The wicked desire a net, while the root of the righteous yieldeth fruit
The wicked yield fruit, while the righteous set nets
medium.explanation: The wicked desire a net of evil men, but the root of the righteous yields fruit.
medium.q: What is the contrast between the wicked and the righteous in verse 12?

medium.explanation: The transgression of his lips snares the wicked.
medium.q: How does sinful speech affect the wicked?

answers: A return or reward for one’s actions
medium.explanation: Recompense is the result or repayment that returns to a person.
medium.q: What does “recompense” mean in verse 14?

answers: Both picture a good source producing beneficial results
challenge.explanation: The righteous root yields fruit, and good speech produces satisfaction.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the root of the righteous and the fruit of the mouth?

answers: A person receives the result or reward of his actions
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the result of a person’s hands returns to him.
challenge.q: What does “shall be rendered unto him” imply?

answers: The snare brings danger, while the fruit brings good
The snare brings satisfaction, while fruit represents deceit
challenge.explanation: Transgressing lips create a snare, while good words produce good.
challenge.q: What is the difference between a snare and fruit in these verses?

answers: The fool who trusts his own way
easy.explanation: The verse says, “he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise.”
easy.q: Who is wise according to verse 15?

easy.explanation: A fool’s wrath is “presently known.”
easy.q: When is a fool’s wrath known?

easy.explanation: The passage compares harmful speech to “the piercings of a sword.”
easy.q: What are the words of one who speaks rashly like?

answers: He turns it into false testimony
medium.explanation: A prudent man “covereth shame.”
medium.q: What does a prudent man do with shame?

answers: The first sheweth righteousness, while the second shows deceit
The first wounds, while the second heals
medium.explanation: The truthful speaker shows righteousness, but a false witness shows deceit.
medium.q: What is the difference between a truthful speaker and a false witness?

medium.explanation: The image describes words that wound people like sword thrusts.
medium.q: What does “speaketh like the piercings of a sword” mean?

answers: Listening to counsel, restraining shame, and speaking truth
challenge.explanation: Wisdom listens to counsel, prudence covers shame, and truthful speech shows righteousness.
challenge.q: What form of self-control is praised in verses 15–17?

answers: A willingness to hear counsel is a mark of wisdom
Counsel belongs only to the wicked
challenge.explanation: The verse directly identifies the person who hearkens to counsel as wise.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between counsel and wisdom?

answers: Sword-like speech versus the healing tongue of the wise
challenge.explanation: Harmful speech pierces like a sword, but the tongue of the wise is health.
challenge.q: What verbal contrast appears in verse 18?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The lip of truth shall be established for ever.”
easy.q: What shall be established for ever?

easy.explanation: The counsellors of peace have joy.
easy.q: Who has joy?

easy.explanation: Lying lips are called an abomination to the LORD.
easy.q: What is an abomination to the LORD?

answers: Truth endures, while a lying tongue lasts only briefly
Falsehood endures, while truth quickly fades
medium.explanation: The lip of truth is established forever, but a lying tongue is only for a moment.
medium.q: What is the difference between truth and falsehood in verse 19?

answers: In the heart of those who imagine evil
medium.explanation: Deceit is in the heart of them that imagine evil.
medium.q: Where is deceit found according to verse 20?

medium.explanation: Those who deal truly are his delight, meaning they please the LORD.
medium.q: What does “his delight” mean in verse 22?

answers: Truth endures, peace brings joy, and honest people please God
Lies are presented as the path to life
challenge.explanation: The verses unite truth, peace, and faithful conduct with endurance, joy, and God’s approval.
challenge.q: How do verses 19–22 reinforce one another?

answers: Evil imagined in the heart produces deceit, while truth is expressed by the lips
Only speech matters, not the heart
challenge.explanation: Deceit begins in the heart of those who imagine evil and is expressed through lying.
challenge.q: What connection is made between the heart and the lips?

answers: One describes false speech, while the other describes faithful conduct
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts lying lips, which God abhors, with truthful conduct, which delights Him.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between “lying lips” and those who “deal truly”?

easy.explanation: A prudent man “concealeth knowledge.”
easy.q: What does a prudent man do with knowledge?

easy.explanation: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule.
easy.q: What shall bear rule?

easy.explanation: A good word maketh the heart glad.
easy.q: What maketh the heart glad?

answers: The diligent bear rule, while the slothful come under tribute
The slothful rule, while the diligent fail
medium.explanation: The diligent bear rule, but the slothful shall be under tribute.
medium.q: What is the contrast between the diligent and the slothful?

answers: The prudent conceal knowledge, while fools proclaim foolishness
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts quiet prudence with the foolishness openly proclaimed by fools.
medium.q: How are prudence and foolishness contrasted in verse 23?

medium.explanation: A diligent person works steadily and persistently.
medium.q: What does “diligent” mean?

answers: Both show wise restraint and purposeful action
challenge.explanation: The prudent control what he reveals, while the diligent steadily works toward responsibility and authority.
challenge.q: What do the prudent and the diligent have in common?

answers: A good word that brings gladness
challenge.explanation: A good word maketh the heavy heart glad.
challenge.q: What remedy for heaviness is presented in verse 25?

answers: Wisdom does not need to boast, while folly reveals itself
There is no difference between wisdom and folly
challenge.explanation: The prudent person quietly keeps knowledge, whereas the fool openly displays foolishness.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between concealing knowledge and proclaiming foolishness teach?

paragraphs.title: The Advantage of the Righteous and the Way of Life

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour.”
easy.q: Who is more excellent than his neighbour?

easy.explanation: The way of the wicked “seduceth them,” or leads them astray.
easy.q: What does the way of the wicked do?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “In the way of righteousness is life.”
easy.q: What is in the way of righteousness?

answers: The slothful wastes what he catches, while the diligent man’s substance is precious
The diligent man refuses to work
medium.explanation: The slothful does not roast his catch, but the substance of the diligent man is precious.
medium.q: What is the contrast between the slothful hunter and the diligent man?

medium.explanation: The way of the wicked seduces or misleads them.
medium.q: How does the way of the wicked affect them?

medium.explanation: A pathway is a way or road; here it pictures the course of righteousness.
medium.q: What does “pathway” mean in verse 28?

answers: What is gained through diligent and upright work is valuable and lasting
Work has no relationship to provision
challenge.explanation: The passage values the substance of the diligent and contrasts it with waste and misleading ways.
challenge.q: What connection is made between diligence, honesty, and security?

answers: The advantage of the righteous and the way of life versus the misleading way of the wicked
The wealth of the wicked versus the honor of the righteous
challenge.explanation: The righteous have advantage and life, while the way of the wicked leads them astray.
challenge.q: What final contrast summarizes verses 26–28?

answers: The path of righteousness leads to life rather than death
Every path ends in death in the same way
The wicked lead the righteous to life
challenge.explanation: The closing statement presents righteousness as a life-giving path without death.
challenge.q: What does “in the pathway thereof there is no death” mean?
